assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experiments and theory showing how electrons tunnel over long distances through protein media, with distance and driving-force dependence stated in physical terms and tested with ruthenium-modified proteins and time-resolved kinetics. It underpins our understanding of respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer and is a clear mechanistic principle in biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit is two names with a coherent, sustained program, so a two-person prize is straightforward. Wider theoretical foundations (Marcus-type theory, tunneling-pathway models) were already recognized or lie outside the listed names; I would want the expert report to confirm priority relative to other protein ET groups.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of confirmation, many independent reproductions, stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as an application of already-recognized electron-transfer theory rather than a new discovery.
Whether Gray's wider bioinorganic work could be conflated with the specific long-range ET contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, and later reprogramming of codons and ribosomes, gave a general chemical tool to place new chemistry in proteins in living cells. Original, clear and widely used, with strong impact on mechanistic enzymology and protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the orthogonal pair approach in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to multiple codons, evolved ribosomes and animals. Mehl and Yokoyama have strong claims too, so the three-laureate limit leaves some unresolved credit; my selection reflects the decisive conceptual and expansion steps.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation; the method is routine in many labs, and applications keep maturing.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is contestable.
Which part is judged the discovery: single-codon incorporation or genome-scale recoding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure calculation with atomic motion, making bond breaking, proton transfer and condensed-phase chemistry accessible from first principles. A clean, original method with enormous lasting impact; as a physicist by training I value its generality and clarity.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper has exactly two authors, and the supplied credit matches, so attribution is unusually clean.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, with widespread independent implementation and a stable interpretation; recognition is timely at the latest.
uncertainties: Computational method prizes sometimes compete with experimental fields on the committee's agenda.
Parrinello also appears in other candidacies, which could complicate how credit is spread.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allows diffraction-before-destruction structures of otherwise intractable membrane proteins and time-resolved structural movies of reactions. It makes dynamic chemical processes visible in 3D, which I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of principle and the methods, Fromme the photosystem and membrane-protein sample work, Hajdu the diffraction-before-destruction concept. Schlichting's time-resolved contributions and others are plausible alternatives, so credit is distributed across many people.
assessment.maturity: The method has been repeated at several XFELs and used for time-resolved studies; mechanistic biology results are still accumulating, so recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Dependence on large facilities and a team effort with many contributors.
Whether time-resolved mechanistic payoffs are mature enough; priority among the pioneers needs expert-report check.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coupling proton and electron movement is central to cytochrome oxidase, photosystem II and fuel-forming catalysis. Experimental thermochemistry and theory of PCET created a unifying chemical framework, close to my own field of proton transfer, with strong impact on molecular electrocatalysis.
assessment.attribution: Mayer (bond-weakening and concerted PCET), Nocera (model systems and energy applications) and Hammes-Schiffer (theory) are decisive; Meyer's early work is a priority concern. This is a line of work rather than a single discovery, which makes fair attribution harder.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across inorganic, biological and computational studies; conceptual framework is stable and still growing.
uncertainties: Rests on a line of work with overlapping contributors, including Meyer.
Whether the committee sees an identifiable single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase explain biological nitrogen fixation at the FeMo cofactor, a fundamental problem of chemical mechanism in living systems. Structures made the cofactor visible, and spectroscopic, kinetic and later cryo-EM work addresses the catalytic cycle.
assessment.attribution: Rees (first FeMo-protein structures and cofactor structure), Einsle (central carbide and ligand-binding states), Seefeldt (kinetic and spectroscopic mechanism); Dean and Ribbe are also strong. The structural credit and mechanistic credit lie with different people.
assessment.maturity: The structure is firmly established; the substrate-reduction mechanism is still debated, so the mechanistic part is not fully mature.
uncertainties: Catalytic mechanism at the cofactor is not settled.
Credit is split between structure and mechanism groups, and more than three people are plausible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel ideas explain how proteins fold by a physical principle, linked with experimental mapping of folding transition states through phi-value analysis. Conceptually deep and physical, with major impact on biophysical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic share the funnel theory; Fersht provides the experimental mapping. Bryngelson and Dill have priority claims, so it is a theory-plus-experiment configuration with some contested credit.
assessment.maturity: The theory is widely accepted, and later computation and AlphaFold-era work changed the context of the folding problem; the principle is mature.
uncertainties: Priority among Bryngelson, Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill.
Relevance after structure prediction advances changes how the committee views impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional and relaxation-based solution NMR methods allowed structure and dynamics determination of larger biomolecules, including methyl-TROSY for very large complexes, giving physical access to motion linked to function.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay shape the isotope-labeled multidimensional methods and dynamics; Wagner and Palmer are plausible alternatives. Ernst and Wuthrich already received prizes in NMR, which complicates novelty for committee members.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, broadly adopted; timing is not an issue, but the method-versus-application framing is.
uncertainties: Prior NMR Nobel prizes reduce perceived novelty.
Allocation among Bax, Clore, Kay, Wagner and Palmer is uncertain.
